instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Acknowledge the Disrespect
cards.instruction: Make someone apologize for the disrespect to your position, not merely for what happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start the apology again, please. You interrupted the chair when you spilled that tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry about your trousers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That covers the cleaning. Now address the interruption of the chair. One complete sentence, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry I interrupted you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The chair. Please use the title; we've already dealt with my trousers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You called the head trainer an idiot in front of the trainees. We'll correct that before tomorrow's drill.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry your drill failed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wrong subject. The apology is for undermining their head trainer. Draft that sentence, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll email it after the drill.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before. Read it aloud before I blow the whistle. I'd like them taking instructions from their head trainer, not the idiot you announced.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Secure the Endorsement
cards.instruction: Get a visible endorsement that makes your decision or position harder to challenge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please endorse the new rota into this microphone. 'Fine' needs to go on the meeting record.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I already told you it was fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Privately. That isn't an endorsement the staff can check. State which rota you're supporting, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I email you instead?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Attach the rota and copy the whole staff. Please don't send me another endorsement only I can see.

beats.text: Sign beside 'I support the extension,' please. A tick without a name won't survive an objection.

cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Delegate Downward
cards.instruction: Make someone accept an unwanted responsibility by placing them lower in the hierarchy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As junior coordinator, you're responsible for the blocked sink. Book a plumber, please, not another volunteer with a coat hanger.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ran the whole event yesterday. You said I'd earned a promotion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: To senior coordinator. You still report to me; now you can supervise the plumber instead of merely booking him.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He can only come after everyone leaves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then keep the keys and lock up afterward. Check every exit, please. I shouldn't have to leave you a junior's checklist.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're my deputy. Draft the replies to the inspector's complaints, please, and keep them factual.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Most of them concern decisions you made.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which you are not being asked to remake. You're handling the complaints below decision-making level. Please stay within the brief.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The inspector wants whoever signs the replies at tomorrow's hearing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sign them, then. Put 'Deputy' under your name, clearly. I don't want your attendance mistaken for a change in senior management.

cards.title: Find the Real Authority
cards.instruction: Probe until you know who can approve, block, or reverse the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I book this coach, identify who can stop the payment, please. Approval and available money are separate checks.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The committee approved it. Book now or we'll lose the coach.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've answered the first check. Who can refuse the deposit? A name, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The treasurer. She's away, but her deputy has the bank login.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Access isn't authority. Can the deputy release the deposit without her permission? That's the answer I need before I book.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The pipe's still leaking. Show me which signature releases the repair money, please, not who has merely seen the form.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All three. I've spent all morning getting them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Completed signatures, yes. Released funds, not yet. Who can still freeze the payment?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Finance. They unfroze the roof payment when the caretaker called.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then check what he said. Did he authorise payment or call someone who could? Please don't book a repair on the strength of a successful phone call.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Build a Coalition
cards.instruction: Recruit someone to your side so your position appears broader and more legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sit beside me for the allotment shed vote. A proposal needs supporters at the table, not scattered nods.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if everyone gets a key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Every plot holder, yes. Let's put the access rule in the proposal before you endorse it. Precision first, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The new plot holders need to hear that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring them to our table. I'll explain the key rule; you introduce them as fellow proposers. Please don't leave them looking like an audience.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Join my request to keep the pottery room open late. One name is a personal request; we need a properly represented proposal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I leave at five.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly why I need you. An evening-class petition only proves the evening class wants longer hours. Put your class beside your name, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The morning class wants weekend access.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then change the heading to 'Extended access' and bring their representative. One proposal, please; don't split our support into two little complaints.
